title: Jira vs Plane
comparison_markdown:
# Jira vs Plane (2026)

## Overview
Jira and Plane are two project management tools that help teams track and manage their work. This comparison is useful for teams currently using Jira who are considering switching to Plane, possibly due to the core use case of issue tracking and project management, and the key reason to switch being the desire for more control over their data and costs. Teams who value customization and self-hosting may benefit from this comparison.

## Key Differences
* Cost: Jira charges per user, while Plane is free and self-hosted.
* Data ownership: Plane allows teams to own their data, while Jira stores data on its servers.
* Setup complexity: Jira has a more complex setup process, while Plane is relatively simple to set up.
* Scalability: Jira is designed for large teams, while Plane is suitable for smaller teams.
* Integration: Jira has a wider range of integrations with third-party tools, while Plane has limited integrations.

## Pricing Comparison
| Aspect | Jira | Plane |
|--------|----------|---------|
| Base Cost | $7.75-$14.50/user/month | Free (self-hosted) |
| License | Proprietary | Apache 2.0 |
| Self-hosting | Not available | Available |
| Per-user cost at 50 users | $387.50-$725/month | $0 (server cost only) |
| Per-user cost at 200 users | $1,550-$2,900/month | $0 (server cost only) |

## Pros and Cons
**Jira:**
* Pros:
	+ Wide range of integrations with third-party tools
	+ Scalable for large teams
	+ Robust project management features
	+ Mobile apps for on-the-go access
	+ Strong customer support
* Cons:
	+ Expensive, especially for large teams
	+ Complex setup process
	+ Limited customization options
	+ Data stored on Jira's servers
**Plane:**
* Pros:
	+ Free and self-hosted
	+ Simple setup process
	+ Customizable
	+ Data ownership
	+ Open-source
* Cons:
	+ Limited integrations with third-party tools
	+ Limited scalability
	+ Limited mobile access
	+ Limited customer support
	+ May require technical expertise for setup and maintenance

## When to Choose Each
Jira is a good choice for large teams that require robust project management features, a wide range of integrations, and strong customer support. It is also suitable for teams that are willing to pay a premium for these features. On the other hand, Plane is a good choice for small to medium-sized teams that value customization, data ownership, and cost-effectiveness. It is also suitable for teams with technical expertise who can handle the setup and maintenance of a self-hosted solution.

## Migration Path
1. Export your Jira data in CSV or JSON format.
2. Use a migration tool, such as the Plane migration script, to import your data into Plane.
3. Configure your Plane instance to match your Jira setup, including workflows, fields, and permissions.
4. Test your Plane instance to ensure that everything is working as expected.
5. Train your team on the new Plane system and provide support during the transition.

## Our Take
Plane is not yet production-ready for most users, as it lacks some of the features and polish of Jira. One specific technical limitation worth knowing is that Plane has limited support for complex workflows and custom fields. However, for small to medium-sized teams that value customization and cost-effectiveness, Plane is a viable alternative to Jira, and we recommend considering it as an option.

## Who Should Switch
* Small teams (less than 10 users) who do not need advanced project management features
* Teams who value data ownership and customization
* Teams with technical expertise who can handle setup and maintenance
* Teams who are currently using Jira's free plan and need more features
* Teams who are looking for a cost-effective solution and do not need integrations with third-party tools

## FAQ
### Is Plane free?
Yes, Plane is free and self-hosted.
### Can I migrate my Jira data to Plane?
Yes, you can export your Jira data in CSV or JSON format and import it into Plane using a migration tool.
### Is Plane suitable for large teams?
No, Plane is not suitable for large teams, as it lacks some of the features and scalability of Jira.
### Does Plane have mobile apps?
No, Plane does not have mobile apps, but it can be accessed through a web browser on mobile devices.
### Is Plane open-source?
Yes, Plane is open-source and licensed under the Apache 2.0 license.

title: Trello vs WeKan
comparison_markdown:
# Trello vs WeKan

## Overview

Trello is a visual kanban board tool from Atlassian, simple and beginner-friendly. WeKan is an open-source kanban board offering the same card/list/board model without vendor dependency.

## Key Differences

- **Cost**: Trello paid plans start at $5/user/month; WeKan is completely free
- **Data control**: WeKan runs on your own server; Trello data lives on Atlassian infrastructure
- **Features**: Trello has a larger Power-Ups marketplace; WeKan covers core kanban features
- **Setup**: Trello requires zero setup; WeKan requires a server
- **Customization**: WeKan open-source code can be extended; Trello cannot

## Pricing Comparison

| Aspect | Trello | WeKan |
|--------|-------------------------------|-------------------------------|
| Base pricing | Free / $5+/user/month | Free (self-hosted) |
| License | Proprietary | MIT |
| Self-hosting | Not available | Available |
| Cost at 50 users | See pricing page | $0/month (self-hosted) |
| Cost at 200 users | See pricing page | $0/month (self-hosted) |
| Vendor lock-in | High | None |

## Pros and Cons

### Trello

**Pros:**
- Polished, professionally designed user interface
- Large ecosystem of official integrations
- Managed infrastructure with no server maintenance required
- Enterprise SLA and dedicated support available
- Mobile apps are well-maintained and reliable

**Cons:**
- Significant per-user monthly cost that scales linearly with team size
- Your data is stored on the vendor infrastructure
- No ability to inspect or modify the source code
- Feature roadmap controlled entirely by the vendor
- Risk of pricing changes, acquisition, or discontinuation

### WeKan

**Pros:**
- Free to self-host with costs only for server infrastructure
- Complete data ownership and privacy control
- Source code is auditable and modifiable
- Active open-source community
- No vendor lock-in or risk of sudden pricing changes
> GitHub: [wekan/wekan](https://github.com/wekan/wekan) * ~20k stars

**Cons:**
- Requires technical knowledge to self-host and maintain
- May lack some advanced features found in the proprietary version
- Support relies on community forums rather than a paid helpdesk
- UI polish may lag behind the proprietary tool
- You are responsible for updates, backups, and security patches

## When to Choose Each

**Choose Trello if:** Trello suits individuals and small teams wanting instant zero-setup kanban with integrations to Slack, Google Drive, and GitHub.

**Choose WeKan if:** WeKan is ideal for teams wanting full data ownership or air-gapped deployments.

## Migration Path

Export Trello boards as JSON, then use WeKan Trello importer in Settings to recreate boards, lists, and cards.

## Our Take

WeKan is production-ready for most teams willing to invest a few hours in setup. The self-hosted version gives you identical or better functionality to the paid Trello tiers, with no recurring per-seat cost.

The main technical limitation worth knowing: you are responsible for your own backups, updates, and uptime. If your server goes down, so does your WeKan instance. Plan for this with automated backups and a monitoring alert.

Our recommendation: if your team has at least one developer and you are paying more than $100/month for Trello, switching to self-hosted WeKan will pay for itself within the first month. If nobody on your team is comfortable with Linux or Docker, stay on Trello until you have that resource.

## Who Should Switch

- Startups under 20 people paying per-seat fees they cannot yet justify
- Dev teams who already self-host other tools and have the ops knowledge
- Organizations in jurisdictions with strict data residency requirements
- Teams who have evaluated Trello paid features and only use the basics
- Founders and solopreneurs who want the functionality without the subscription

## FAQ

### Is WeKan free to use?
Yes. WeKan is free to self-host. Your only cost is the server, typically $6-$12/month on a VPS provider like DigitalOcean or Vultr.

### How hard is it to migrate from Trello to WeKan?
For most teams, migration takes 2-4 hours. Export your Trello data, follow the WeKan import guide, and test with a small group before switching everyone over.

### Does WeKan get regular updates?
Yes. WeKan has an active open-source community with regular releases. Check the GitHub repository for release frequency.

### Can I use WeKan without technical knowledge?
You need basic comfort with a VPS and command line. If that feels unfamiliar, there are managed hosting options that handle the server for you at a modest cost.

### What happens if WeKan development stops?
Because the source code is open, you can continue running whatever version you have indefinitely. You can also fork the project or switch to another tool at your own pace — no vendor can shut off your instance.

---
*Data sourced July 2026. Pricing and features change. Verify at [Trello](https://trello.com) and [WeKan](https://wekan.github.io) before making decisions.*

For most teams, migration takes 2-4 hours. Export your Dropbox data, follow the Nextcloud import guide, and test with a small group before switching everyone over.

### Does Nextcloud get regular updates?
Yes. Nextcloud has an active open-source community with regular releases. Check the GitHub repository for release frequency.

### Can I use Nextcloud without technical knowledge?
You need basic comfort with a VPS and command line. If that feels unfamiliar, there are managed hosting options that handle the server for you at a modest cost.

title: Linear vs Plane

# Linear vs Plane (2026)

## Overview
Linear and Plane are two project management tools designed to help teams organize and track their work. This comparison is beneficial for teams currently using Linear who are considering switching to Plane, possibly due to the core use case of needing more control over their data or a more customizable solution. The key reason someone would switch is to leverage Plane's self-hosted option and open-source nature.

## Key Differences
* Cost: Linear offers a free plan and charges $8 per user per month for its paid plan, while Plane is free and self-hosted.
* Data Ownership: Plane allows teams to have full control over their data since it can be self-hosted, whereas Linear stores data on its servers.
* Setup Complexity: Plane requires more technical expertise to set up, especially for self-hosting, compared to Linear's straightforward sign-up process.
* Scalability: Both tools can scale, but Plane's self-hosted nature means teams have to manage their own server resources.
* Integration Difference: Linear has a more comprehensive set of integrations with third-party services out of the box, while Plane may require more manual setup for similar functionality.

## Pricing Comparison
| Aspect | Linear | Plane |
|--------|----------|---------|
| Base Cost | Free / $8/user/month | Free (self-hosted) |
| License | Proprietary | Apache 2.0 |
| Self-hosting | Not available | Available |
| Per-user cost at 50 users | $400/month | $0 (server cost only) |
| Per-user cost at 200 users | $1,600/month | $0 (server cost only) |

## Pros and Cons
### Linear
* Easy to set up and use
* Comprehensive set of integrations
* Scalable
* User-friendly interface
* Limited control over data storage
### Plane
* Self-hosted option for full data control
* Open-source and customizable
* Scalable with proper server management
* Free
* Requires technical expertise for setup and maintenance

## When to Choose Each
Linear is suitable for teams of all sizes that prioritize ease of use and a wide range of integrations. It's ideal for teams who do not have the technical resources to manage a self-hosted solution and are comfortable with a proprietary tool. Plane, on the other hand, is best for teams that value data ownership and customization. It's particularly suited for larger teams or organizations with the technical capability to manage their own servers and require a high degree of control over their project management tool.

## Migration Path
1. Export your data from Linear in CSV or JSON format.
2. Set up your Plane server, either on your own hardware or through a cloud provider.
3. Use Plane's import tool to migrate your data from the exported Linear files.
4. Configure any necessary integrations or customizations in Plane.
5. Test your setup to ensure all features and data are properly migrated.

## Our Take
Plane's production readiness for most users is currently limited by its requirement for technical expertise to set up and maintain, especially for smaller teams. A specific technical limitation worth considering before switching is the need to manage server resources, which can add complexity and cost. For teams prioritizing data control and customization, and having the technical capabilities to support a self-hosted solution, switching to Plane can be beneficial.

## Who Should Switch
* Small teams of less than 10 users who prioritize data ownership and do not need extensive integrations.
* Medium-sized teams of 10-50 users who have the technical resources to manage a self-hosted solution and value customization.
* Large teams or enterprises with over 50 users who require high scalability and full control over their data.
* Teams in highly regulated industries who must comply with specific data storage and security regulations.
* Development teams who prefer an open-source solution for project management.

## FAQ
### Can I self-host Linear?
No, Linear does not offer a self-hosting option. 
### Is Plane completely free?
Yes, Plane is free and open-source, but teams will need to consider the cost of server resources for self-hosting.
### Does Plane have the same integrations as Linear?
Not yet, Plane's integration ecosystem is still developing and may require more manual setup for some services.
### Can I migrate my data from Linear to Plane directly?
Yes, you can export your data from Linear and import it into Plane using its import tool.
### Is Plane suitable for small teams with no technical expertise?
Not recommended, Plane requires technical expertise for setup and maintenance, making it less suitable for small teams without such resources.

* Scalability: Microsoft Teams is designed for large-scale deployments, while Mattermost is also scalable but may require more configuration.
* Integration: Microsoft Teams has native integration with Microsoft Office tools, while Mattermost has integration with a wide range of third-party tools through its open API.

## Pricing Comparison
| Aspect | Microsoft Teams | Mattermost |
|--------|----------|---------|
| Base Cost | Free / $6-$22/user/month | Free (self-hosted) |
| License | Proprietary | MIT / AGPL |
| Self-hosting | Not available | Available |
| Per-user cost at 50 users | $6-$22/user/month (approximately $300-$1,100/month) | $0 (server cost only) |
| Per-user cost at 200 users | $6-$22/user/month (approximately $1,200-$4,400/month) | $0 (server cost only) |

## Pros and Cons
**Microsoft Teams:**
* Pros:
	+ Easy to set up and use
	+ Native integration with Microsoft Office tools
	+ Large user community and support resources
	+ Scalable and reliable
	+ Wide range of features and integrations
* Cons:

title: Google Workspace vs Nextcloud

# Google Workspace vs Nextcloud

## Overview

Google suite of cloud productivity tools including Gmail, Drive, Docs, Sheets, Meet, and Calendar. is a popular proprietary tool in the productivity space. Nextcloud is a free, open-source alternative that gives organizations complete control over their data and deployment.

## Key Differences

- **Cost**: Google Workspace costs $6-$18/user/month; Nextcloud is Free (self-hosted)
- **License**: Google Workspace is Proprietary; Nextcloud is AGPL 3.0
- **Data ownership**: Nextcloud can be self-hosted so your data stays on infrastructure you control
- **Vendor lock-in**: Nextcloud eliminates dependency on a single commercial vendor
- **Community**: Nextcloud has an active open-source community contributing features and fixes

## Pricing Comparison

| Aspect | Google Workspace | Nextcloud |
|--------|-------------------------------|-------------------------------|
| Base pricing | $6-$18/user/month | Free (self-hosted) |
| License | Proprietary | AGPL 3.0 |
| Self-hosting | Not available | Available |
| Cost at 50 users | ~$300/month | $0/month (self-hosted) |
| Cost at 200 users | ~$1,200/month | $0/month (self-hosted) |
| Vendor lock-in | High | None |

## Pros and Cons

### Google Workspace

**Pros:**
- Polished, professionally designed user interface
- Large ecosystem of official integrations
- Managed infrastructure with no server maintenance required
- Enterprise SLA and dedicated support available
- Mobile apps are well-maintained and reliable

**Cons:**
- Significant per-user monthly cost that scales linearly with team size
- Your data is stored on the vendor infrastructure
- No ability to inspect or modify the source code
- Feature roadmap controlled entirely by the vendor
- Risk of pricing changes, acquisition, or discontinuation

### Nextcloud

**Pros:**
- Free to self-host with costs only for server infrastructure
- Complete data ownership and privacy control
- Source code is auditable and modifiable
- Active open-source community
- No vendor lock-in or risk of sudden pricing changes
> GitHub: [nextcloud/server](https://github.com/nextcloud/server) * ~27k stars

**Cons:**
- Requires technical knowledge to self-host and maintain
- May lack some advanced features found in the proprietary version
- Support relies on community forums rather than a paid helpdesk
- UI polish may lag behind the proprietary tool
- You are responsible for updates, backups, and security patches

## When to Choose Each

**Choose Google Workspace if:** Google Workspace is the right choice when you need the most polished user experience, the broadest integration ecosystem, and professional support with SLA guarantees.

**Choose Nextcloud if:** Nextcloud is ideal for privacy-conscious teams, organizations with strict data sovereignty requirements, or anyone wanting to eliminate per-seat subscription costs.

## Migration Path

Export your data from Google Workspace in its standard export format, review Nextcloud import documentation, and plan a pilot period where both tools run in parallel.

## Our Take

Nextcloud is production-ready for most teams willing to invest a few hours in setup. The self-hosted version gives you identical or better functionality to the paid Google Workspace tiers, with no recurring per-seat cost.

The main technical limitation worth knowing: you are responsible for your own backups, updates, and uptime. If your server goes down, so does your Nextcloud instance. Plan for this with automated backups and a monitoring alert.

Our recommendation: if your team has at least one developer and you are paying more than $100/month for Google Workspace, switching to self-hosted Nextcloud will pay for itself within the first month. If nobody on your team is comfortable with Linux or Docker, stay on Google Workspace until you have that resource.

## Who Should Switch

- Startups under 20 people paying per-seat fees they cannot yet justify
- Dev teams who already self-host other tools and have the ops knowledge
- Organizations in jurisdictions with strict data residency requirements
- Teams who have evaluated Google Workspace paid features and only use the basics
- Founders and solopreneurs who want the functionality without the subscription

## FAQ

### Is Nextcloud free to use?
Yes. Nextcloud is free to self-host. Your only cost is the server, typically $6-$12/month on a VPS provider like DigitalOcean or Vultr.

### How hard is it to migrate from Google Workspace to Nextcloud?
For most teams, migration takes 2-4 hours. Export your Google Workspace data, follow the Nextcloud import guide, and test with a small group before switching everyone over.

### Does Nextcloud get regular updates?
Yes. Nextcloud has an active open-source community with regular releases. Check the GitHub repository for release frequency.

### Can I use Nextcloud without technical knowledge?
You need basic comfort with a VPS and command line. If that feels unfamiliar, there are managed hosting options that handle the server for you at a modest cost.

### What happens if Nextcloud development stops?
Because the source code is open, you can continue running whatever version you have indefinitely. You can also fork the project or switch to another tool at your own pace — no vendor can shut off your instance.

---
*Data sourced July 2026. Pricing and features change. Verify at [Google Workspace](https://workspace.google.com) and [Nextcloud](https://nextcloud.com) before making decisions.*
